It seems like [this call](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/27443bf16ecadf5ba16fd3cd4305e49930dec8e8/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/repository/GitCloner.java#L294) to [urlPathSegmentEscaper()](https://google.github.io/guava/releases/19.0/api/docs/com/google/common/net/UrlEscapers.html#urlPathSegmentEscaper()) escapes `/` as `%2F`, causing the generated archive URL to become
`https://github.com/user%2Frepo%2Farchive%2Ftag.tar.gz` (returns an HTTP 404 error) instead of
`https://github.com/user/repo/archive/tag.tar.gz` (expected)

I [updated](https://github.com/akira-baruah/bazel/commit/448117adaa32f39c0639182e263eed54f49531ac) `GitClonerTest` to verify the GitHub download URL, and sure enough, the `/` characters are incorrectly escaped:
```

Actual invocation has different arguments:
httpDownloader.download(
    [https://github.com/foo%2Fbar%2Farchive%2F1.2.3.tar.gz],
    "2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9826",
    Optional.of(tar.gz),
    /home/akira/.cache/bazel/_bazel_akira/e36bf307e80952c206a5da49e956330b/bazel-sandbox/3032536169757988015/execroot/io_bazel/_tmp/84a104db675a04ee2341dbc170478a33/output-dir,

```
Compare:
1) `https://github.com/foo/bar/archive/1.2.3.tar.gz` (expected)

body:
`bazel build @git_repo//...` now works for the example provided above. NOTE that the GitHub checksum has changed to `c18f281fd6621bb264570b99860a0241939b4a251c9b1af709b811d33bc63af8`:

```
# WORKSPACE

git_repository(
    name = "git_repo",
    commit = "e3bd4cbeaeef3cee65a68a8bd3c535cb779e9b6d",
    remote = "https://github.com/google/googletest.git",
    sha256 = "c18f281fd6621bb264570b99860a0241939b4a251c9b1af709b811d33bc63af8",
)

http_archive(
    name = "http_repo",
    sha256 = "c18f281fd6621bb264570b99860a0241939b4a251c9b1af709b811d33bc63af8",
    strip_prefix = "googletest-e3bd4cbeaeef3cee65a68a8bd3c535cb779e9b6d",
    url = "https://github.com/google/googletest/archive/e3bd4cbeaeef3cee65a68a8bd3c535cb779e9b6d.tar.gz",
)
```

There's a bug that [breaks downstream projects](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/commit/cf52ebad2f794b0c9c7fb6b77e57937bb76f53da). Here's what I think causes it:

GitHub usually prefixes archive contents with a directory named `<repo>-<reference>` where `<repo>` is the repository name and `<reference>` is a commit, branch, or tag.

However, there's an exception to this rule when a tag is formatted as a version like `v1.2.3`. In this case, GitHub omits the initial "v" producing a prefix like `<repo>-1.2.3`. For example running

    `curl -L https://github.com/bazelbuild/rules_docker/archive/v0.3.0.tar.gz | tar xvz`

yields `rules_docker-0.3.0/` instead of `rules_docker-v0.3.0`.

issue.body:
Addresses #3661 and fixes #3770 bug

Changes:
- Properly escape the download URL. `GitCloner` used to incorrectly escape `/` delimiters as `%2F`. This change was originally introduced in #3770 but [rolled back](https://github.com/akira-baruah/bazel/commit/58c003cf98b81d433603eeeb3874c7dbba33e1f0) due to a bug that is now fixed below.
- Omit an initial "v" from a version tag (e.g. `v1.2.3`) in the archive prefix. GitHub seems to do this.

body:
The CI server references
[`https://ci.bazel.io/blue/organizations/jenkins/PR%2Fbazel-tests/activity`](https://ci.bazel.io/blue/organizations/jenkins/PR%2Fbazel-tests/activity)
with only this single slash escaped and
[`https://ci.bazel.io/blue/organizations/jenkins/PR/bazel-tests/activity`](https://ci.bazel.io/blue/organizations/jenkins/PR/bazel-tests/activity)
gives HTTP 404 error.

1) Why is only this single slash escaped?
2) Why does the un-escaped URL not work?

@Androbin I think that Jenkins constructs its URL as `https://{address}/blue/organizations/<org_name>/<pipeline_name>/activity` and in this case, the pipeline is named `PR/bazel-tests` (as opposed to something like `abseil-cpp`). Since the `/` in the pipeline name isn't acting as a URL delimiter, it is properly escaped as part of the pipeline name field.

So, to answer your question:
1. The single slash is escaped because it is part of a field and is not a delimiter.
2. If that slash is not escaped, it's parsed as delimiter, creating two separate fields (e.g. `PR` and `bazel-tests`) when there's actually only one (e.g. `PR/bazel-tests`).

Please let me know if you see any issues or if any of this doesn't make sense. Thanks!
@damienmg since 7459a2117709ba927ed80f70233397598918dfa0 has been merged, should we close this issue?
Right I don't know why this issue was still open.
I think the original PR message only said "addresses #3661" (which is not a [GitHub closing keyword](https://help.github.com/articles/closing-issues-using-keywords/)).
